body:
## Summary

References #363, items 1 and 2 only. Item 3 (what a flag's extract contains) is untouched -- it is a design question reserved for the owner.

- **Item 1 -- newest at the top.** The owner decided this on 2026-08-13 ("Most recent at the top, older at the bottom is easy, simple design language"); this builds it. New rows now insert at the top of the live view instead of the bottom, and Autoscroll holds `scrollTop` at 0 instead of chasing `scrollHeight`. `rendered`/`groups` stay oldest-first internally -- the frozen-pool logic and `groupEvents`' "head is the first arrival" rule both depend on that order -- and display order is inverted once, at the last step before the template renders it (`displayRendered`/`displayGroups`, a `.reverse()` of a `.slice()` copy). A group that's hit again still does not move.
- **Item 2 -- measure what Group mode compresses.** `live-group-mode.mjs` only ever asserted direction (never more rows) and honesty (counts add up); nobody had measured a ratio. Added a scenario that does, against three distinct traffic shapes (see below). Group mode's behaviour is unchanged -- this is measurement only.

## Item 1 -- proving the hard property

The scrolled-back-reader property ("a reader who turned Autoscroll off still sees a pixel-stable view") is the part worth being skeptical of, per this project's own history of vacuous scroll assertions (`scrollHeight === clientHeight` making "scrolled to the bottom" trivially true). `frontend/scripts/live-newest-first.mjs` proves it in a real browser:

- Confirms real overflow first (`scrollHeight` vs `clientHeight` vs `window.innerHeight`), so the rest of the scenario isn't measuring a clipped, non-scrolling box.
- Confirms the newest event renders first and Autoscroll holds `scrollTop` at 0.
- Turns Autoscroll off, scrolls to `scrollTop=400`, snapshots the title of the 10 rows currently in the DOM.
- Feeds 60 more events while frozen, then re-checks: `scrollTop` is pixel-identical, and the same 10 rows in the same order are still there -- not just "row count unchanged," but the *same* rows at the *same* positions.
- Confirms none of the events fed while frozen appear anywhere.
- Turns Autoscroll back on and confirms it resumes at the top with the newest event.

`frontend/src/components/LiveTable.svelte.test.ts` adds two jsdom tests pinning display order (deliberately *not* asserting anything about `scrollTop`/`scrollHeight` there -- jsdom reports 0 for both regardless of what the component does, which is exactly the vacuous-assertion shape to avoid). Both were confirmed to fail against the unfixed component before the fix (via `git stash`) and pass after.

## Item 2 -- measured compression

No real RouterOS capture is available in this environment, so the scenario (`frontend/scripts/live-group-compression.mjs`) brackets the answer with three traffic shapes rather than inventing one blended number:

| Shape | Rows before -> after | Reduction |
|---|---|---|
| Repeated identical connection (a blocked host retrying the same target), n=200 | 200 -> 1 | 99.5% |
| Port scan (one source/dest, 200 distinct ports), n=200 | 200 -> 200 | **0.0%** |
| Generic traffic (`live-env.sh`'s own round-robin `syslog` generator), n=300 | 300 -> 250 | 16.7% |
| Combined, n=700 | 500 -> 450 | 10.0% |

The honest finding: Group mode earns its place on the case it was built for (one connection hammered repeatedly), but a port scan -- arguably the more attention-grabbing pattern -- gets **zero** compression, because the grouping key is source+destination+port+protocol+action and port is deliberately part of it (the owner's "golden group" decision, #363/#341). Worth knowing, not flattering, reported as measured.

## Other changes

- `docs/screenshots/live-view-{dark,light}.png`: regenerated against a real running instance, so they show newest-at-top rather than the pre-#363 bottom-appending behaviour.
- `frontend/scripts/capture-live-view-screenshots.mjs` (new, **not** a live-check scenario -- named outside the `live-*.mjs` glob so `make live-check` doesn't pick it up): the existing `tools/screenshots/{capture.mjs,gen_traffic.py}` predate authentication becoming mandatory and the plaintext syslog listener's removal (#189), so neither runs against current `dev` as-is. This reuses the same traffic mix/IP pools but drives it through the already-working TLS ingest path and does a real login. Left the two existing files untouched -- fixing them fully is separate, unscoped work.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: behaviour-change entry under `Unreleased/Changed`.

## Scope

Not touched: the setup wizard, `main.go`, `internal/api/`, `internal/engine/`, `internal/store/`, `internal/syslog/`, `.github/workflows/` -- each is owned by a parallel effort right now.

## Verification

- `npx svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.app.json` (frontend/): 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `npx vitest run` (frontend/): all tests pass.
- `gofmt -l $(git ls-files '*.go')`: clean (no Go files touched).
- `make live-check`: full suite passes, including both new scenarios. One unrelated flake observed on this run, `live-flags-clearing.mjs` (a flag-arrival timing wait unrelated to the live view/grouping) -- not touched by this PR, and reproduced independently of these changes across several runs in this shared environment.

Does not close #363 -- item 3 remains open.
title: Live view: newest event at the top, and measure Group mode's real compression
